newsitem.title: GERMANY: German companies slam higher TV ad time prices.
newsitem.headline: German companies slam higher TV ad time prices.

text.p: OWM, the association of German companies that advertise, attacked television channels on Thursday for hiking rates for advertising time during tough economic times.
"Ad price increases, which lead to more money being paid for the same services, threaten to throw the advertising business out of balance," the OWM said in a statement.
Top German commercial television stations Sat1, ProSieben and the RTL network announced ad price hikes of an average of five percent for 1998 at the beginning of August.
Public stations, which are not allowed to show ads after 8 p.m., rejected the increases as ARD froze prices and ZDF dropped them.

The OWM said that it had spoken with the private stations earlier in the summer to inform them of the extraordinary weakness of the current consumer goods market, which they said had drained their advertising budgets.
The group said that if the price increases were the result of spots during prime time being sold out, lifting the German restriction on ads on after 8 p.m. on public stations ought to be considered.
